speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; to understand the cause, can you tell me how long it has been there and if you have any history of diabetes or vascular disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your history of DVT and chronic swelling, have you noticed any skin discoloration (like brown staining) or changes in texture on that leg?

REQUEST TEST: Duplex_Ultrasound
REQUEST IMAGES: Right_lower_leg_photograph

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Duplex_Ultrasound findings indicate evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in the superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg. Right lower leg photograph shows a large ulcer with surrounding skin discoloration consistent with chronic venous changes (pigmentation).

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CUI) with Venous Leg Ulcer.

The ultrasound confirms venous reflux and obstruction, and the photos show the classic ulcer with surrounding pigmentation. Since you have a history of DVT and family members with similar leg issues, this aligns perfectly with hereditary venous disease leading to stasis ulcers. Do you have any active bleeding or signs of infection, such as warmth or pus, in the wound?
